## Implementation plan: issue #9423, a CI fix on PR #8307 (`orchestrator/project-8291`)

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `da76ba7b293a37a3a551fcdb2a59183b3ef73752`, branch `orchestrator/project-8291` (integration branch, mismatch = false). `scripts/dependency_wait_resume.py` is not on the default branch (`isolated-base`); it exists only on this integration branch.

## Files likely to change
- `scripts/dependency_wait_resume.py`
- `tests/test_dependency_wait_resume.py`

- `changelog.d/stuck-states-p8d-generic-seed.md`

## Functions or modules to implement
1. In `scripts/dependency_wait_resume.py`, lines 71-83, add `"ai:workflow-heal-escalated"` as the last member of the frozenset `SEED_HUMAN_LATCH_LABELS`. Rewrite the comment above it to say the set is the union of `workflow_failure_heal.HUMAN_NEEDED_LABELS` and `orchestrate_lib.STALL_RECOVERY_LATCH_LABELS`. Keep the existing reason for copying instead of importing (the helper runs as `python3 -I`) and the note that a parity test keeps them aligned. Add a short note that `ai:workflow-heal-escalated` (#9248) is deliberately left out of `HUMAN_NEEDED_LABELS`, because that tuple drives the heal-intake `if:` predicates. Change nothing else. `seed_candidate()` at line 638 already reads this set, so the skip covers the new label without any logic change.
2. In `tests/test_dependency_wait_resume.py`, line 799, inside `test_seed_human_latch_labels_cover_repo_latch_sets`, replace the equality with:
   `assert dwr.SEED_HUMAN_LATCH_LABELS == set(workflow_failure_heal.HUMAN_NEEDED_LABELS) | set(orchestrate_lib.STALL_RECOVERY_LATCH_LABELS)`
   Keep lines 800-801 as they are. The parametrized test at line 779 (`sorted(dwr.SEED_HUMAN_LATCH_LABELS)`) picks up the new label automatically. It checks that an issue carrying the label is not seeded, and that it is seeded once the label is removed.
3. Two unreleased fragments on this integration branch describe the seed set as "seven labels" and "the same labels as `HUMAN_NEEDED_LABELS`", which will no longer be true. The rule allows editing existing text to correct it, and both fragments belong to this project:
   - `agents.d/stuck-states-p8d-generic-seed.md`: add `ai:workflow-heal-escalated` to the label list. Say the set is the union of `HUMAN_NEEDED_LABELS` and `STALL_RECOVERY_LATCH_LABELS`. Keep the `<!-- agents: section=... -->` marker exactly as it is.
   - `changelog.d/stuck-states-p8d-generic-seed.md`: change "all seven human-latch labels" to eight, add `ai:workflow-heal-escalated`, and replace the "same labels as `HUMAN_NEEDED_LABELS`" sentence with the union description. Keep the `<!-- changelog: fixed -->` header.

## Data structures affected
- `dependency_wait_resume.SEED_HUMAN_LATCH_LABELS` (a frozenset constant) grows from 7 to 8 members. No schema, marker, env var or log value changes.

## API or interface changes
- None. The `outcome=` and `seeded=` log values are unchanged, and no new GitHub API call is added (the check reads the existing call-1 label snapshot).
- `workflow_failure_heal.HUMAN_NEEDED_LABELS` and both heal-intake workflow `if:` predicates are deliberately left alone.

## Decisions
### D1 — Widen the seed set, not HUMAN_NEEDED_LABELS
- Chosen: add `ai:workflow-heal-escalated` only to `SEED_HUMAN_LATCH_LABELS`, and redefine the parity test as a union.
- Alternatives considered: add the label to `workflow_failure_heal.HUMAN_NEEDED_LABELS`; or drop the subset assertion at line 800.
- Why: `HUMAN_NEEDED_LABELS` is pinned to the `if:` predicates in `workflow-templates/ai-workflow-failure-heal.yml` and `.github/workflows/internal-workflow-failure-heal.yml`. Adding the label there would send heal escalations back into the heal intake and also require workflow edits. Dropping the subset assertion would hide real drift. The union keeps both relationships enforced.

### D2 — Correct the existing P8d fragments in the same PR
- Chosen: update the label lists in the unreleased agents.d and changelog.d fragments.
- Alternatives considered: leave them stale; or add a new fragment.
- Why: those two files would otherwise describe the behaviour wrongly once they are folded in at release. Editing existing text is allowed, and a second fragment would contradict the first.

## Security considerations
- No trust boundary, endpoint, credential or external input is touched. The change only makes seeding stricter: one more human latch stops automatic `/answer` posting, which fails closed.
- Abuse case closed by the fix: before it, an issue that heal had escalated (`ai:workflow-heal-escalated`) but that was also `ai:blocked` with `Depends on: #N` could be seeded and later auto-answered past the human latch. After the fix it is skipped.
- No money handling is involved.

## Potential risks or edge cases
- If `HUMAN_NEEDED_LABELS` or `STALL_RECOVERY_LATCH_LABELS` change again, the union equality will flag drift in either direction, which is intended.
- Issues already seeded that carry `ai:workflow-heal-escalated` are not changed, because the skip only applies when seeding. This matches how P8d treats the other latches.
- Open PRs #9219, #9134 and #9278 touch `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py`. If any of them changes `HUMAN_NEEDED_LABELS`, the union test will expose it. No conflict is expected, because this plan does not edit that file.
- The issue's claims match the checkout: `orchestrate_lib.py` lines 1624-1628, `dependency_wait_resume.py` lines 71-83, and test lines 799-801 all agree with what the issue describes.

## Testing considerations
- Run `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python -m pytest tests/test_dependency_wait_resume.py -q`. Expect `test_seed_human_latch_labels_cover_repo_latch_sets` to pass and the new parametrized case `test_seed_skips_every_human_latch_label[ai:workflow-heal-escalated]` to pass.
- Run `tests/test_agents_fragment_contract.py` and `tests/test_changelog_fragment_contract.py` to confirm the edited fragments still satisfy their marker and header contracts.
- No workflow YAML changes, so the workflow file size guard does not apply.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends dependency_wait_resume.SEED_HUMAN_LATCH_LABELS
Scope-mode justification: The fix extends the existing seed-latch constant and its parity test exactly as the triage suggested, with no new helper, call or interface. Updating the two P8d fragments costs a few lines and keeps the documentation correct. Applying the "Boil the Lake" rule, the complete option is chosen because completeness moves correctness, which ranks above speed in §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed). `HUMAN_NEEDED_LABELS` and the workflow predicates are left alone on purpose, as D1 explains.
